extracted.intended_audience: UKRI and DSIT senior leaders, board members, sponsorship and governance teams, accounting officers, and other officials responsible for governance, finance, audit, and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: A formal governance and accountability framework describing the roles, responsibilities, duties, standards and reporting requirements that UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and its sponsor department (DSIT) must follow. It sets strategic objectives, required governance arrangements, reporting, audit, risk and assurance practices, and procedures for dispute resolution and winding-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework purpose and review frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: This framework document sets out the broad governance framework within which UKRI and DSIT will operate, their core responsibilities, and how the day-to-day relationship works in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document should be reviewed and updated at least every 3 years unless exceptional reasons agreed with HM Treasury and the Principal Accounting Officer prevent this; minor updates (e.g., name changes) may be made at the discretion of the relevant Director with agreement of the UKRI CEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI must operate subject to and complementary with legal and regulatory requirements, in particular the Higher Education and Research Act (HER Act), Managing Public Money (MPM), delegation and Accounting Officer letters from DSIT, and other Cabinet Office and HM Treasury instructions/rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI must have regard to guidance issued by DSIT and comply with any directions from the Secretary of State; references to UKRI include subsidiaries and joint ventures classified to the public sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic objective: Protect and promote basic curiosity-driven research
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect and promote basic curiosity-driven research through a long-term, sustainable funding model underpinning the UK research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes funding outstanding basic research (growing from SR25 baseline), increasing opportunities for multi- and interdisciplinary research, minimising bureaucracy and administrative barriers, improving financial sustainability (including HE reform), and managing research infrastructure sustainably to meet strategic needs and maximise regional economic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic objective: Align portfolio with government priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure UKRI’s portfolio is aligned with delivering the government’s priorities, including the 5 missions and industrial strategy, to deliver UK-wide impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design portfolios that communicate measurable outcomes, leverage private sector investment (target 3:1 over 5 years where appropriate), complement wider government investments across departments, and communicate outcomes in ways that resonate with the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic objective: Provide targeted innovation and commercialisation support
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide targeted innovation, commercialisation and scale-up support across the UK to drive economic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support innovative R&D firms and scale-ups, simplify access to finance and support, maximise value of research data (ethical, safe, reducing bureaucracy), deliver regional innovation funding, and ensure incentives at lower TRLs to encourage exploitation and maximise economic return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic objective: Deliver local impact and enhance collaboration, security and resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver local impact and enhance national and international collaboration, security and resilience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider regional growth in investments, ensure access for diverse researchers, establish global partnerships, support research strengthening defence/security, and foster a security culture protecting people, information and assets through grant assessment, procurement and facilities access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic objective: Develop and sustain R&D environment and talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and sustain an R&D environment supporting national science capability and attracting and nurturing research and innovation talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support talent at all career stages, enhance diversity of research career opportunities, embed R&D reforms delivering high-quality research and innovation, consolidate UKRI as effective organisation with continuous improvement culture, encourage pro-innovation culture and new funding/delivery/evaluation methods, and ensure work benefits citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and status
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI is classified as a central government organisation by ONS/HM Treasury and administratively as an executive non-departmental public body (NDPB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification informs applicable governance, reporting and sponsor relationships; changes to subsidiaries/joint ventures require documented arrangements agreed with DSIT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes under HER Act
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI’s primary purposes are to advance knowledge, improve lives and drive growth across the UK through its activities and through partners it funds, and to support higher education providers via Research England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory purposes flow from establishment under the HER Act and frame UKRI’s functions and permitted activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory duties and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under HER Act section 93 UKRI may carry out, facilitate, encourage and support research, development, exploitation, knowledge exchange, dissemination, promotion, advice and awareness activities in science, technology, humanities and new ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI must have regard to using resources effectively, efficiently and economically and to other guidance from DSIT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to minimise bureaucracy
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI has a mandate to have due regard for reducing bureaucracy in all new initiatives and programmes it funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This derives from government response to the Review of research bureaucracy and should inform programme and process design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance and accountability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall operate corporate governance arrangements that accord with good corporate governance practice and applicable regulatory requirements and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: comply with Corporate Governance in Central Government Departments Code of Good Practice (or explain departures in annual report), comply with MPM, have regard to relevant Functional Standards (Finance, Commercial, Counter Fraud, Analysis, Grant and Project Management), and take into account codes/guidance in Annex A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual governance statement and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall provide an account of corporate governance in its annual governance statement, including the Board’s assessment of compliance with the Code and explanations of material departures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intending to materially depart from the Code, UKRI should notify the sponsor in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial powers and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State (DSIT) is accountable to Parliament for UKRI, with powers including appointment of Board members/senior roles, power to give directions, amend council structures/fields of activity via regulations, request/agree strategy, make grants with terms and conditions, require information/advice and direct representation in international relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Day-to-day oversight is delegated to the Science Minister; ministerial powers are exercised consistent with HER Act and other statutory frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to give directions and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The HER Act provides the Secretary of State with power to give directions to UKRI; this will be exercised proportionately, e.g., in response to serious financial management issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of State will consult UKRI before issuing directions, will publish directions as soon as possible (no later than in next governance statement), CEO must inform Board at next meeting, and lessons should be learned from the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with directions and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI should comply, or respond if they cannot comply, with any guidance falling short of a direction from the Secretary of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In issuing directions the Secretary of State will have regard to specified issues (paragraph 15.2) and to statutory constraints (e.g., Research England functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Accounting Officer (PAO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PAO (Permanent Secretary) designates the UKRI Chief Executive as Accounting Officer and is accountable to Parliament for grant-in-aid; PAO advises on objectives, budgets and monitors UKRI performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAO ensures AO is aware of responsibilities, issues AO appointment letter, advises Secretary of State, monitors risks, informs UKRI of policy, brings concerns to UKRI Board, ensures training on AO responsibility and supports CEO in discharging responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO modes of intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: PAO may intervene to ensure AO duties are fulfilled, potentially including withdrawal of delegated AO responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervention mechanisms include: negotiations on corporate plan, withdrawing/changing delegated authorities (respecting Haldane principle), advising Secretary of State to remove Board members, attaching conditions to grants, requiring more frequent financial reporting/assurance, and contributing to performance appraisal of Board/CEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship team role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI Sponsorship Team in DSIT is the primary day-to-day contact maintaining an effective two-way relationship: championing UKRI within government and supporting/challenging UKRI to deliver effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorship tasks include informing UKRI of policy/guidance, engaging on cross-government priorities, presenting funding allocation advice to Secretary of State, advising on performance targets, liaising on approvals, monitoring performance and expenditure, acting on significant problems, coordinating DSIT asks, advising on appointments/remuneration, and maintaining information requirement lists reviewed quarterly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership principles
rubrics_metrics.description: DSIT and UKRI commit to an open, honest, trust-based partnership based on clear accountability, mutual understanding of strategic aims and recognition of unique capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitments include: clearly designated roles without duplication, keeping each other informed of significant issues, focus on policy outcomes, support and challenge on policy/practice, open communication including risk-sharing, proportionate oversight tailored to risk, prompt issue resolution, acting with integrity/honesty/objectivity/impartiality, and ensuring security risk assessment at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Haldane principle and application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Haldane principle (decisions on individual research proposals are best taken following evaluation of quality and likely impact, e.g., peer review) should be respected; HER Act defines its application for science and humanities councils and Research England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic, long-term decision-making requires input from subject-matter experts and central government; the Haldane principle does not apply to government funding of innovation or Innovate UK activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual support, balanced funding and devolved funding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary of State must consider the balanced funding principle when determining allocations between the two components of the dual support system and apply Barnett Formula adjustments to devolved administrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research England’s allocation is determined by Secretary of State; devolved administrations decide whether to make equivalent grants to support research/knowledge exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI will achieve effective communications impact from funded work and work closely with DSIT for ministerial involvement in announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI should provide ministers opportunities to be involved in significant announcements, give DSIT advance sight of funding announcements for joint planning, and ensure branding acknowledges government funding; publicly funded research conclusions must be communicated independently without political restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: DSIT access and attendance at meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: The HER Act gives the Secretary of State or DSIT officials a right of attendance at UKRI Board meetings and committees (except the Executive Committee) with access to papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSIT will attend meetings when this aids deliberations; the Executive Committee may invite Secretary of State or representative to attend as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution process
rubrics_metrics.description: DSIT and UKRI will adopt a pragmatic, issue-based approach to resolving disputes, using this framework and other high-level governance documents as reference points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalation: identify issues early, use routine sponsorship meetings for day-to-day issues, escalate within organisations at working level, then to Directors, Director General, PAO; PAO may ask Permanent Secretary to nominate Non-Executive Member to review/mediate; once resolved, record lessons learned and communicate guidance internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a FOI or data protection request is received by either party, the receiving party will consult the other prior to any disclosure of information that may affect the other party’s responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers FOI Act 2000 and Data Protection Act 1998/2018 requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal risk and litigation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall provide quarterly updates to the sponsor on any active, threatened or reasonably anticipated litigation and agree protocols for substantial litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation protocols must ensure timely reporting and protection of legally privileged information; until agreed, material developments must be communicated promptly, privileged documents marked, and circulation of privileged information limited to necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting Officer (CEO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Executive as Accounting Officer is personally responsible for safeguarding public funds, ensuring propriety, regularity, value for money and feasibility, and for day-to-day operations and management of UKRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEO must ensure UKRI is run to standards set out in MPM (Box 3.1), sign accounts, prepare governance statement, ensure complaint handling procedures meet Ombudsman principles, act in accordance with legislation, framework document, delegation and settlement letters, and maintain internal mechanisms for monitoring compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO responsibilities to DSIT
rubrics_metrics.description: CEO must establish corporate and business plans in agreement with DSIT, inform DSIT of progress against policy objectives, provide timely forecasts and monitoring, notify on likely overspends, ensure adherence to ministerial budget allocations, maintain delegated authorities and personnel policies, and ensure Council Executive Chairs receive annual appraisals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEO must ensure timely information for monitoring performance is supplied to both UKRI Board and DSIT.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO duty to establish assurance and control systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO will establish a system of controls and assurance to ensure Accounting Officer responsibilities are fulfilled and to demonstrate to the PAO that UKRI has an effective assurance framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should facilitate clear accountability, effective governance, decision-making and financial management across UKRI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board committees and minimum governance structures
rubrics_metrics.description: As a minimum, UKRI’s Board should establish an Audit and Risk Assurance Committee and a Nominations and Remuneration Committee; other sub-committees may be established as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees should be set up in accordance with the Code of Good Practice for Corporate Governance and the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, business plans and management information
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI must provide business plans, financial reporting, management information and updates on progress, delivery of objectives and value for money to DSIT, including quarterly updates and publication of evaluation outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSIT-UKRI shared list of information requirements should be reviewed annually and at Quarterly Governance and Assurance meetings; timely forecasts and notifications of significant problems are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data protection and GDPR obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, DSIT and UKRI are separate Controllers and must comply with data protection legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, ensure nominated Data Protection Officers are in place, notify nominated officers of breaches without undue delay, and have processes to notify the ICO within 72 hours when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall establish and maintain internal audit arrangements in accordance with Public Sector Internal Audit Standards (PSIAS) and ensure DSIT is satisfied with competence of the Head of Internal Audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI must set up an audit committee, forward audit strategy/periodic plans/annual audit report and Head of Internal Audit opinion to DSIT per agreed timeframe, keep records and report on fraud/theft, share audit information affecting departmental responsibilities, and provide internal audit with right of access to all documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: External audit and NAO/C&AG arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller & Auditor General (C&AG) audits UKRI’s annual accounts; UKRI must send statements of accounts to the Secretary of State and the C&AG and normally lay accounts pre-summer recess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C&AG examines, certifies and reports on statements; C&AG has statutory access to documents and may carry out examinations into economy, efficiency and effectiveness; UKRI should provide for C&AG access to grant recipients' documents as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews and winding-up arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: DSIT will put in place arrangements for orderly winding up of UKRI if required, ensuring assets and liabilities pass to a successor or revert to DSIT and that closing accounts and audits are arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should specify valuation and accounting treatment of assets/liabilities, ensure independent assurance on transactions and financial commitments, arrange for external audit of closing accounts, and identify who signs closing accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex A: compliance with specified guidance and codes
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall comply with the listed guidance, documents and instructions (e.g., Corporate Governance Code, Code of Conduct for Board members, Managing Public Money, FReM, Orange Book, PSIAS, procurement guidance, public appointments codes, Treasury guidance on senior pay, fraud/error/debt guidance, IPA project guidance, Government Digital Service etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is non-exhaustive and UKRI has a duty to keep abreast of changes to government operational policy and legal requirements; specific named documents set out further detailed obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and cyber requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI must foster a positive security culture that protects people, information and assets and take steps to ensure basic cyber security controls are in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security should be considered at each stage (including sharing information outside DSIT/UKRI); basic cyber security controls should be at least at the Cyber Essentials scheme level and other relevant government cyber guidance should be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum DSIT-UKRI formal meeting schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A minimum number of formal meetings are required between DSIT and UKRI to support sponsorship and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: monthly meetings between UKRI CEO and DSIT Director General (Science, Innovation & Growth Group); quarterly progress and performance meetings with senior teams and DSIT finance leads; Quarterly DSIT-UKRI Assurance meeting chaired by Sponsorship deputy; responsible Minister will meet regularly with Board/Chair/CEO as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI must ensure risks are captured, escalated and communicated speedily and effectively and carry out risk assessments proportionate to level of risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk processes should align with departmental risk assessment, inform DSIT periodically at a frequency proportionate to risk, and be integrated into monitoring, reporting and assurance frameworks.
